content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** Flagged as a **deviation** against the IP rule, targeted at the fallback level.

- **§7.0 Materials (p0082–p0086)** is the operative deliverables IP regime. Materials default to **Type II** (IBM-owned) if not otherwise specified, and our Type II licence is only "irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up ... within Customer's Enterprise only" — no perpetual term, no modification right, no sublicensing. §14.17 forecloses any implied licence, so the fallback licence elements fail on material terms.
- **§14.18 Data Protection (p0204)** allowed IBM and its Enterprise to store and use our contact data anywhere they do business and pass it to contractors, Business Partners and assignees for promotions and marketing research — independent exploitation of Customer data rather than service delivery.

Two surgical replacements: (1) add *perpetual*, *royalty-free*, *modify* and *sublicense* and replace the Enterprise-only restriction with "for Customer's business", leaving IBM's Type II ownership sentence untouched (already-met element); (2) confine IBM's use of our contact information and all other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for us to processing solely to provide the Services. The Type I licence-back in §7.b was left alone as outside this checklist.
